report.title: docs: --trusted-proxies and --rate-limit are missing from the environment variables reference
report.body:
### Check before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate

### What problem would this solve?

Rate limiting is on by default since #6315, and the client address it uses depends on `--trusted-proxies` (`MEMOS_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, default `private`). Neither that option nor `--rate-limit` (`MEMOS_RATE_LIMIT`, default `true`) appears in the [environment variables reference](https://usememos.com/docs/configuration/environment-variables) or the [reverse proxy guide](https://usememos.com/docs/deploy/reverse-proxy). Both are bound in `cmd/memos/main.go`, and the only description I found is the design note `docs/design/api-abuse-controls.md`.

This matters most to the people following the reverse proxy guide, who can't tell from the docs that they may need to set it. According to that design note:

- If the proxy sits on a public address and isn't listed, forwarding headers are ignored and the proxy's address counts as the client, so everyone behind it would share one rate-limit bucket.
- If other hosts on the private network are untrusted, or the instance is reached through a NAT hop that presents a private peer address without rewriting headers, a client can forge `X-Forwarded-For` and get a fresh per-address bucket. These operators are told to set `none` or list the real proxy.

### What would you like to happen?

- Add both options to the table in `configuration/environment-variables`, in `usememos/dotcom`.
- Add a short note to `deploy/reverse-proxy` covering when to change the `private` default, using the two cases above.

The docs repo doesn't appear to take outside changes, so I'm filing this here. I can draft the text if that's useful.

### Additional context

I found this by reading the code and docs. I didn't run a deployment to observe either case, so the behavior above is as the design note describes it.

This issue was prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude Code).
